Subject: Quantix redlines (MSA + Order Form) — productization & training concerns

Neha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We circulated the draft MSA + order form through our legal and product teams and attached a single PDF with tracked redlines (Quantix_Redlines_MSA_OrderForm_20270815.pdf). High-level concerns from our side:

- Output ownership: we need explicit language that prevents Redwood from claiming title to customer-generated outputs when those outputs are created entirely from Quantix-provided prompts and data.
- Model retraining / derived training: we cannot agree to open-ended training rights. Any use of our data for model updates must be opt-in and subject to a separate agreement.
- Feedback license: acceptable to provide ephemeral telemetry for performance improvements, but must be anonymized and cannot be used to reproduce our proprietary prompts/products.

Attached are suggested edits. We tried to offer compromise language in a couple places (see §4.2 and §7.1 of the redline).

Can you confirm receipt and let us know how Redwood typically handles: (a) productization carveouts, (b) evidence/evidence requests for provenance, and (c) a two-week timeline for commercial sign-off? We also looped procurement for any PO timing questions.

Alex
Legal Counsel | Quantix Health

Subject: RE: Fwd: Quantix redlines — proposed legal approach

Thanks for the forward — I reviewed the redlines and drafted a short list of proposed counterpoints. High-level position below; see inline comments in the attached PDF for exact wording.

1) Output ownership / title
- We should accept a narrow carveout: Quantix retains title to outputs that are solely created from Quantix-provided proprietary data and prompts ("Customer-Originated Outputs").
- However, we must preserve a broad license to use outputs for debugging, service improvement, and to operate the service. Proposed language: "Customer-Originated Outputs shall remain the Customer's property; Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use such outputs solely to provide the service, to debug and to improve service reliability; Redwood shall not assert ownership of Customer-Originated Outputs."

2) Training / derived models
- We cannot accept a total bar on retraining. Instead, propose: (a) Redwood will not use Customer-Originated Outputs or Customer-submitted PII for model retraining without Customer's prior written opt-in; (b) Redwood may use aggregate, de-identified telemetry for model quality monitoring.
- Offer a paid "Training Opt-In" addendum: customer may pay an agreed fee for limited retraining privileges, with guardrails.

3) Feedback license / telemetry
- Strongly recommend explicit anonymization and a prohibition on storing raw prompts tied to customer identifiers.
- Proposed telemetry language: "Redwood may collect anonymous usage telemetry and aggregated model performance metrics; such telemetry shall not include raw customer prompts or outputs tied to identifiable Customer data."

4) Evidence & provenance requests
- Quantix asked for provenance evidence on model outputs. Operationally, we can provide logs and token-level trace for a limited retention window under an NDA and subject to a narrow scope.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi to confirm commercial trade-offs (price uplift or one-time fee for 'Training Opt-In');
- I will prepare redline suggestions and a short rationale memo for the sales/exec thread;
- Neha to propose a 30-min legal + procurement call with Quantix to align on non-negotiables.

Laura Bennett

- Offer Training Opt-In as a paid add-on: one-time integration fee + monthly premium based on model retrain frequency. Example pricing: $25k onboarding + $5k/month for limited retrain access (TBD by usage).
- For telemetry/feedback: propose 'aggregate-only' default; offer a separate technical escrow / analytics feed under NDA for customers who need traceability (chargeable).
